[NDBG.14.4.2] `asserter.kind` is one of:

- `"rule"` — a firing asserted it: `{ "kind": "rule", "rule_name": "sensor_absorb", "firing": "!12", "clock_ns": 1000000000 }`;
- `"input"` — the trace, a fact file or an inject fed it ([NDBG.14.13]);
- `"response"` — it is a call's answer ([LCRS.4.3.1]);
- `"engine"` — the engine asserted it itself, as it does a fault fact
  ([LERR.9]).

Each kind other than `"rule"` carries `kind` and `clock_ns`.

`retractor` is `null` if the fact is still live. `retractor.kind` is one of
`"rule"` (a firing retracted it), `"ttl_expiry"`, `"support_lost"` (a
logical fact whose last support ended) and `"input"` (the trace, a fact file
or an inject withdrew it). For `"rule"`, `retractor` also carries `rule_name`
and `firing`. The fact breakpoint's retract reasons are these kinds
([NDBG.12.3.2]).
